pr_title: Limit number of alerts or series produced by a rule
pr_body:

This PR adds support for a group-level limit of the number of alerts produced by an alerting rule or series produced by a recording rule. If the limit is exceeded, the active alerts are removed if it's an alerting rule, and the rule returns an error which subsequently sets the health to bad.


Fixes #9225
pr_comments:
@roidelapluie would you mind giving this another review / merge?
We'd love to vendor this into Loki as well.
The code looks fine, but I need to take this in real situations to really assess the behavior end-to-end. I'll do it asap.

I have run some tests, it works as expected.  One thing surprised me: we do not report evaluation errors in the /alerts page, only in the /rules page.

I wonder if we should add more documentation. With this setting, an alert can simply never fire if it directly hit the threshold. This is reflected on prometheus_rule_evaluation_failures_total, which we could mention as well.
Note to self: we should also note that after getting back below the limit, the alert need to go via the for: duration again.
Mmh this pull request takes into consideration the "inactive alerts", which are not pending and not firing. I feel like they should not count, WDYT?
I will merge and we will iterate over an issue.

Is there a reason for introducing a single parameter limiting both the number of alerts and series a rule can generate? For context, we would like to limit just the number of alerts a rule can generate in Grafana Mimir. Would it make sense if we add a new parameter to limit only the number of alerts the rules of a rule group can generate, and potentially a corresponding one limiting the number of of series?

issue_context.title: Limits on the number of alerts generated by a rule
issue_context.body: We have a customer with a faulty rule that generated 30K alerts from a single rule. Now this makes the `/api/v1/rules` API nearly impossible to use with 15MB+ of data. We have scrape time limits on the samples we scrape, but I think we should also have limits on the number of samples each rule evaluation generates.
comments: This would just be a separate query engine `MaxSamples` limit for alerting rules, right?
`MaxSamples` is on the input data and I am thinking of a new limit for the output of the alerting rules.

Yes, I suppose enforcing a limit on `active` alerts (which I believe is the correct output slice) makes more sense. Would we log a warning and send the alerts up to the limit, or error and send none at all? It seems unexpected to completely ignore all alerts if there are too many, but I don't think a log line is noticeable enough. Maybe a new alert state, something like `exceeded`?
I think we should send the alerts up to the limit. But also, this would mean a "failed evaluation" and the error would show up in the UI and alert would be triggered by the mixin.

Should we set the `state` to `HealthBad` or leave it at `HealthGood`? I'm inclined to say `HealthBad` because something is not right.

In order to trigger an alert in the mixin we have expose a new metric, like `rule_evaluation_alerts_exceeded_total`.
We will set it to Bad. I think we can get away with incrementing `prometheus_rule_evaluation_failures_total`
Sounds good! I can work on this.

Shouldn't we do this for rules in general (not just alerting rules, but also recording rules)?

A recording rule producing an exploding amount of output series is a problem, too.
HealthBad since we would not Commit() to tsdb, but Rollback instead, similar to scrape, where we set up = 0 even if the scrape-over-network part works.
I think we should fail completely and not store alerts if we break the limit. The default would still be no limit so we would not break our users.
I agree with failing completely now. If a user received some alerts, they might falsely believe they're getting the full picture.
